sections.html:
Stafford County fronts the Potomac and Rappahannock rivers, facing the City of Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania County across the water. The Washington metro region includes it. Of its 280 square miles, 269 are land. A count of 156,927 people in 2020 has grown to an estimated 170,803 for 2025. Stafford is the seat, and Aquia Harbour is the biggest community.

A Board of Supervisors elected from seven magisterial districts governs the county, with a county administrator running the departments. Naming your district helps pinpoint a property: George Washington, Hartwood, Falmouth, Griffis-Widewater, Aquia, Garrisonville or Rockhill.

Few homes sit empty. The 2020 census found 52,793 housing units with a vacancy of just 3.6 percent, and the rental vacancy rate was 5.2 percent. Homeowners lived in 77.2 percent of occupied units. Children under 18 were in 42.0 percent of the 50,869 households.

sections.h2: Quantico, commuting and your sale date
sections.html:
Marine Corps Base Quantico takes up part of northern Stafford County, with the FBI Academy, the FBI National Laboratory and NCIS headquarters on the Stafford side. Many residents commute north to defense and federal sites, and many military families live here.

Selling because of orders or a deployment? Tell the closing agent your move date at once, and the settlement can be planned around it.

  • Commuters rely on I-95, U.S. 1 and the Virginia Railway Express.
  • Housing on the Quantico post feeds Department of Defense schools instead of the county system.
  • Federal and defense paychecks help explain the county's high household incomes.

I-95's Express Lanes end in Stafford, north of Exit 133. Other major roads are U.S. 1, U.S. 17 and State Routes 3, 212 and 218. Leeland and Brooke are the VRE stations in the county. Congestion is a sore spot, so spell out the drive to the station and the interstate when you describe the house.

A tornado struck southern Stafford in the early hours of May 9, 2008 and damaged about 140 homes. Snow has been heavy too, with roughly 25 inches in December 2009 and about 19 inches in February 2010.

Buyers sometimes ask about roof age, attic insulation and trees after storms like these. A small file of records answers most of it:

  • Proof of any roof replacement or patching.
  • A note of insurance claims paid on the house.
  • Trees trimmed back from the roofline before showings.

Before you call a buyer or an agent, put the following in one place. It will save several rounds of back-and-forth later.

  • Your most recent tax statement and proof of what you have paid.
  • A mortgage statement, if a loan is open, so a payoff can be ordered.
  • Records of storm repairs, roof work and insurance claims.
  • The name of your magisterial district and anything unusual about the lot.
  • Papers showing who is allowed to sign, which matters most for an inherited house.

Colonial history runs deep here, and the National Register lists many properties. Aquia Church, built in 1757, is a National Historic Landmark. Planning exterior work on a house in an older area like Falmouth or Aquia? Check with county planning first to learn whether local review applies.

sections.h2: How does a Stafford County assessment appeal work?
sections.html:
Your first move is a review request to the assessor. If the answer stands, the Board of Equalization is next. The board presumes the assessor got it right, so your job is to prove the valuation exceeds fair market value or lacked uniformity.

  • Owners of homes with fewer than four units may ask in writing for the assessment records, which the assessing officer must hand over within 15 days.
  • When the officer misses that deadline, the records and the valuation method must be presented at your hearing before you speak.
  • Evidence can include sales made through the December 31 before the assessment date, but not later studies.
  • The board can move values up or down whether or not anyone complained.

Errors have their own track. An assessor's mistake, or a factual error during a general reassessment, can be fixed on application. The deadline is the later of three years after the tax year ends and one year after the assessment.

sections.h2: Property tax when a Stafford house sells
sections.html:
Until the treasurer has been paid, the county's lien outranks the rest, which is why back tax is deducted from the sale money. Penalty and interest are part of the debt.

Virginia ruleWhat it means for a Stafford seller
Tax lienBack tax, penalties and interest come out of the sale money
Current-year shareDivided between seller and buyer by the contract
Grantor tax50 cents per $500 of value, paid by the seller unless the buyer agrees to pay
Delinquent tax salePossible after a set number of years unpaid, with 30 days' notice first
Installment planUp to 72 months if the treasurer agrees

The Commissioner of the Revenue values property and the Treasurer collects, and both are elected. Contact each office for your parcel's current status.

sections.h2: Selling when you owe tax or inherited the house
sections.html:
A tax debt is not a barrier to selling. Payment is taken at closing, the lien is lifted, and the remainder is yours. Should the debt top the sale price, consult the treasurer and your closing agent first.

Heirs get extra room. Those who claim ownership through a will or intestacy may request a pause on a tax sale, and installments can run as long as 72 months. Spend that time clearing up title, then choose between keeping the house and selling it as is.

Recording happens at the Stafford County Clerk of the Circuit Court, which collects the grantor tax and requires the sale price on the deed's first page. Before asking for offers, assemble your tax payoff, mortgage payoff and repair records. Buyers can then act without delay.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Stafford
sections.html:
Since a cash buyer needs no mortgage, nothing in the contract hinges on loan approval or an appraisal. The offer comes in writing, and you can measure it against a listing's likely result once repairs and showings are counted. Accept, and a title company hunts for liens and unpaid tax that the closing agent then settles from your proceeds. Closing is usually the last step, and the settlement statement lists every payout.

Two habits save time. Know your own figures: tax balance, mortgage payoff, deed tax. And be open about roof work, storm repairs and insurance claims. A buyer with the full picture prices the house as it is and has nothing to discover later.

faqs.q: Who assesses and who collects property tax in Stafford County?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue values the property, and the Treasurer bills and collects. Phone either office for your parcel's balance and deadlines.

faqs.q: What tax rules apply if I inherit a house in Stafford County?
faqs.a: Unpaid tax follows the house until it is paid. Heirs claiming by will or intestacy may ask the treasurer to hold a tax sale, and installment plans can last up to 72 months.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Stafford County house that I owe tax on?
faqs.a: Yes. Closing pays the tax from your proceeds and the lien is released afterward. If you owe more than the house will bring, see the treasurer and the closing agent first.

faqs.q: Where do Stafford County deeds get recorded?
faqs.a: At the Stafford County Clerk of the Circuit Court. The sale price has to appear on page one, and the grantor tax is collected at recording.

faqs.q: Can I get my assessment records before an appeal?
faqs.a: For a residential property with fewer than four units, yes. Ask in writing, and the assessing officer must deliver the records within 15 days.
